newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up on bargain hunting.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Tuesday on domestic bargain hunting encouraged by rises in the A share market, but it was likely to consolidate in the short term given the absence of overseas funds, brokers said.
The B share index rose 0.331 points or 0.46 percent to 71.623 points on volume of 18.5 million shares worth $9.4 million compared with $9.2 million on Monday.
The A share index stayed on its steady bull course, closing up 6.418 points or 0.51 percent at 1,254.717 points on turnover of 10.2 billion yuan against 12.3 billion yuan on Monday.

Brokers said the index was likely to consolidate in the short term despite rises over the past few days with overseas investors unwilling to build positions in the company reporting season when most firms results remain unclear.
"Some domestic bargain hunting pushed the index up in the absence of foreign funds," one broker said.
"The technical charts seem good, but we need to see rises in trading volume and a good performance by market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui for further rises," a second broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 21 up, four flat and 18 down.
Toy maker Shanghai Haixin was the star on expectations of strong 1996 results, rising $0.036 or 6.54 percent to $0.586 on volume of 694,400 shares.

Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the most on follow-up buying triggered by institutional support, gaining $0.016 or 1.62 percent to $0.998 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index closed firmer on bullish market sentiment, but a technical correction was expected in the short term, brokers said.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index closed up 41.312 points or 1.2 percent to 3482.478 points.
Textile company Shanghai Dragon Head was the star on talk of financial reconstructuring, surging 0.74 yuan or its daily limit-up of 10 percent to 8.11 yuan on volume of 7.9 million shares.
